questions.q: Which epithelium forms the layered band at the surface of this slide?
questions.explain: A band of many cell layers over connective tissue indicates a stratified epithelium; flattening toward the surface makes it squamous.
questions.alt: Low-power view of a thick pink and purple layered epithelium over loose connective tissue containing glands.

questions.q: Which description fits the deepest cells of this epithelium?
options: Small, tightly packed cells forming a darker basal layer
Large dome-shaped cells with two nuclei
questions.explain: The darker band at the base is the basal and parabasal layer, where the cells divide.
questions.alt: Low-power view of a thick pink and purple layered epithelium over loose connective tissue containing glands.

questions.q: Which feature separates this epithelium from transitional epithelium?
options: Flat squamous surface cells replace dome-shaped umbrella cells
questions.explain: Transitional epithelium has large dome-shaped cells at the surface; stratified squamous cells flatten.

questions.q: Which epithelium lines the urinary bladder?
questions.explain: The urinary bladder is lined by transitional epithelium, which changes thickness as the organ fills.
questions.alt: A thin pink band of tissue crosses the middle of a pale field.

questions.q: Which epithelial type forms the thin lining of blood vessels?
questions.explain: The endothelium is a specialised simple squamous epithelium. Its thin, continuous lining permits exchange and provides a surface for blood flow.

questions.q: A tracheal biopsy shows nuclei at different heights, cilia on the free surface and goblet cells. Which epithelium is present?
questions.explain: The respiratory epithelium is pseudostratified ciliated columnar. All cells contact the basement membrane, although not all reach the lumen.

questions.q: Which epithelial adaptation is characteristic of the absorptive surface of the small intestine?
options: Tall simple columnar cells with apical microvilli
questions.explain: Simple columnar enterocytes bear apical microvilli that increase the surface area available for nutrient absorption.

questions.q: Which epithelial type protects the oesophagus from abrasion while remaining moist?
questions.explain: The oesophagus is lined by non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium, which resists friction from swallowed food without a surface keratin layer.

questions.q: A section of an eccrine sweat duct shows two layers of cuboidal cells. Which epithelium lines the duct?
questions.explain: The larger ducts of sweat glands are commonly lined by stratified cuboidal epithelium, typically two cell layers thick.
